chunks: From al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, who said: A man said to Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) while I was with him:

"Indeed, those before us say: When Allah loves a servant, a caller from the heavens declares: 'Allah loves so-and-so, so love him!' So Allah instills love in the hearts of the people. And when He hates him, a caller from the heavens declares: 'Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him!' So Allah instills hatred in the hearts of the people."

He (peace be upon him) was reclining, so he sat upright, then shook his sleeve, and said: "It is not so! But when Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) loves a servant, He incites the people against him so they may say about him what is not true; so He may reward him and punish them. And when He hates a servant, Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) pours love for him in the hearts of the people so they may praise him for what he does not possess, thereby punishing them and him."

Then he said: "Who was more loved by Allah than Yahya ibn Zakariyya? Yet He incited all those you see against him until they did with him what they did. And who was more loved by Allah than al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him)? He incited against him until they killed him! And who was more despised by Allah than Abu So-and-So and So-and-So? It is not as they have said."

key_terms.أَغْرَى: To incite or stir up (people against someone)
key_terms.لِيُؤْثِمَهُمْ: So that He may sin/punish them
key_terms.لِيُؤْجِرَهُ: So that He may reward him

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between divine love and divine hatred in terms of public perception according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith refutes the common belief that divine love results in public acclaim and divine hatred in public scorn. Instead, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) explains that when Allah loves a servant, He incites people to criticize him falsely, thereby rewarding the servant for enduring it and punishing the critics. Conversely, when Allah hates a servant, He incites people to praise him falsely, causing both to be punished for the insincerity.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 18. Al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar narrates: I was with Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (a.s) when a man came to him and said:

“Some people say that when Allah loves a servant, a caller from the heavens will declare, 'Allah loves so-and-so, so love him!' So Allah will instill the love (of him) in the hearts of the servants. But when He hates him, a caller from the heavens will declare, 'Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him!” So Allah will instill the hate (of him) in the hearts of the servants.

He (a.s) was reclining, so he sat upright and said: “It is not so. Rather, when Allah (may His majesty be glorified) loves a servant, He incites the people against him that they may say against him what is not true; and he may thereby be rewarded whilst they may be punished for that. And when He hates a servant, Allah (may His majesty be glorified) pours love for him in the hearts of people so they may praise him for what he does not possess and thereby both they and he may be punished.”

Then he said: “Who was more loved by Allah than Yahya ibn Zakariyya? Yet, all those who were around him were against him until they did with him what they did (i.e. they killed him). And who (also) was more loved by Allah (may His majesty be glorified) than Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (a.s)? People turned against him until they killed him! And who was more despised by Allah than Abu so-and-so and so-and-so? It is not as they have said.”
